transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-30 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45 min | Participants: Maya, Leo, Sam (Redwood) — Priya, Carlos, Rina, Tom, Jules (Arborea)

Summary (auto): Quick scoping call to align on POC success criteria and integration approach.

00:00 - Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, i'm maya from redwood inference, ae on the account.
00:08 - Priya Nair: Hi all, priya here, head of ml at arborea. we do real-time taxonomy tagging across incoming event streams, low latency matters.
00:15 - Tom Bennett: tom, cto—mostly here to make sure platform constraints are clear, vpc, encryption, the usual.
00:22 - Leo Park: leo, se — i'll run through benchmarks and the integration examples.
00:30 - Carlos Mendes: carlos, platform eng; we'll own the benchmark environment and run the load tests.

02:12 - Maya Chen: high level, the ask is a short pilot so you can validate performance + cost on your workload; we want to agree on success criteria — latency p95, throughput, quality thresholds, and then an integration path.
02:25 - Priya: yes. for us success is p95 under 200 ms for the short prompts used in tagging — average token length about 60 tokens, typical prompt shape. and cost needs to be within our ops budget, so we'll measure token unit cost plus infra.
02:40 - Jules: i'd add correctness — we need >92% precision for top label on our eval set.
02:50 - Sam Rivera: good, so we'll capture both latency + quality. for quality, can you share the eval set and a representative sample of prompts?
03:05 - Priya: yes, we'll upload a subset to the shared GCS bucket, and include failure cases.

05:00 - Leo Park: on sizing, can you walk through qps — steady-state and peaks?
05:08 - Carlos: steady is ~20 rps per region, peaks up to 60 rps for short bursts, but the core pilot target we want to validate is 50 qps sustained for 10 minutes.
05:20 - Leo: perfect. that maps to our initial benchmark target. we'll test both hosted and a dedicated config; if you need VPC/private we'll show the private deployment flow but for speed we typically start hosted with customer data controls.

07:15 - Rina Sato: security is critical — we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS support for customer keys, and logs that can be exported to our SIEM.
07:30 - Maya: all standard — we'll send SOC2 and network architecture docs; we have KMS integrations and audit logs. for private mode we support customer-managed keys and VPC peering.

09:05 - Tom: timelines? we're trying to decide between a 2-week spike or a 4-week pilot. what does redwood recommend?
09:12 - Maya: recommended is 4-week pilot: week 0 onboarding + baseline, week 1 benchmarks, week 2 integration and SDKs, week 3 iterate on tuning and final report. but if you have tight timelines we can compress.
09:25 - Priya: 4 weeks sounds about right.

11:00 - Leo: integration options — you can use our OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoints or our native SDKs (python/node). both support function/tool calling and structured JSON output. which do you prefer?
11:15 - Carlos: we want minimal lift. openai-compatible would be easiest to slot into our existing code and tracing.
11:22 - Sam: great — note that our OpenAI-compatible endpoints also support function calling semantics and the same payloads; we also provide example libraries that wrap retries, batching, and streaming.
11:40 - Jules: does function calling support nested JSON schemas? we need a specific JSON schema for the tag object with fields: label, confidence, provenance, evidence_snippet.
11:52 - Leo: yes, you can pass a json schema for structured output. there are some caveats with partial responses and validation — we'll include schema validation in the sample code.

14:00 - Maya: also mention streaming — if you need real-time UI updates we can stream tokens back; for structured outputs we usually buffer until the final schema is emitted to avoid partial parse issues.
14:15 - Priya: that works — our UI expects final object per event.

16:30 - Carlos: about benchmarking — what do you need from us? payload shapes, average token counts, concurrency targets?
16:38 - Leo: all of that — plus any auth patterns, whether you want openai-compatible versus SDK auth. we'll provide a runbook: test harness, synthetic load generator configs, and a script to replay a saved event stream.
16:52 - Carlos: we'll provide sample payloads, and we'll run the harness in our staging VPC and share logs.

19:20 - Sam: quantization/throughput notes — for cost and throughput we recommend a quantized model variant; for your latency target we might pick a 7B quantized model vs a larger model. we'll show kernel/hardware mappings in the benchmark report.
19:35 - Priya: ok, we care about latency more than absolute quality, but we still need that 92% precision; can you run both accuracy and latency comparisons between the quantized and full-precision variants?
19:48 - Leo: yes, we'll include quality regression checks and flag any >2% drop in precision.

22:05 - Tom: network/topology — we'll need VPC peering for private or a private endpoint if we're using hosted. do you support peering + mTLS?
22:15 - Maya: yes, private endpoints and VPC peering available. mTLS supported for private deployments. we'll send the network diagram and required firewall rules.

25:00 - Priya: how about observability — token-level cost, per-route latency, error tracing?
25:08 - Sam: redwood console gives token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and you can pull traces into your tracing system via our tracing hooks. we'll include a screenshot in the doc pack.

27:30 - Jules: about function calling — when we define a function that returns the tag object, can we get structured fallback if model hallucinated? we want deterministic post-processing.
27:40 - Leo: we recommend combining schema validation plus a small post-processor that enforces enum constraints and confidence thresholds; we'll include example code in python.

30:10 - Maya: ok let's circle back on acceptance criteria — summarizing: p95 < 200ms at 50 qps sustained, precision >= 92% on your eval set, integration via OpenAI-compatible endpoint with function-calling + schema, and security reviews completed. anyone want to edit that?
30:28 - Priya: that's good. add cost per 1k tokens target — we have internal threshold, we'll compare after you send pricing.
30:36 - Maya: noted.

33:00 - Leo: operational notes — if you go dedicated we can reserve capacity and guarantee throughput; hosted pilot will be best-effort but usually sufficient for benchmarking. dedicated also gives isolation and predictable latencies.
33:20 - Tom: what's the timeline to spin up dedicated?
33:24 - Maya: dedicated typically needs a 2-4 week lead time for reserved pools; for pilot we usually start hosted, then move to dedicated if results are positive and you want SLA.

36:00 - Carlos: ok for the bench next week — how do we coordinate?
36:07 - Leo: i'll send a benchmark plan with exact endpoints, scripts, and a calendar invite for the 2-hour run.
36:15 - Maya: i'll send pricing and the legal/pilot template.
36:20 - Sam: and i'll push the sdk samples and a small example repo showing openai-compatible calls, function calling examples, and schema validation.

40:00 - Priya: anything else? i just want to make sure credentials and sandbox keys are scoped.
40:05 - Maya: yes, sandbox keys will be scoped to the pilot project and rotated. we'll include auth examples (api key + mTLS for private).
40:15 - Rina: can you include KMS flow diagrams?
40:18 - Maya: yes, included in the security pack.

43:00 - Tom: recap and next steps please.
43:08 - Maya: recap — 4-week pilot, bench target 50 qps / p95 <200ms, precision >=92%, deliverables: pricing, sdk examples, security docs, benchmark plan. action items assigned. schedule benchmark for next week.
43:30 - Priya: great thanks everyone.
43:35 - All: thanks, bye.

(End of transcript)
